messages:
Ana (Product PM): Thanks for the all-hands — a few quick follow-ups on mission/positioning so we can sync comms and docs. @Claire @Raj?
Claire (CEO): Yep, go ahead — happy to clarify.
Ana (Product PM): First: when we say 'serving beats model ownership' — are we framing this as purely cost/latency or also platform lock-in + operability? trying to make a concise line for the website.
Raj (VP Product): Short answer: it's both. emphasize predictable economics, unified runtime, and operational primitives (rollouts, fallbacks). customers care about total cost + reliability + ease of integration.
Sam (Staff Engineer): Also call out predictable latencies — our smart routing + KV cache are real differentiators. tiny bullet for docs: "predictable latency under load".
Emily (Director, Eng): On technical messaging: can we avoid deep infra jargon on marketing pages? translate "KV cache" -> "response caching for repeated prompts" for non-technical audiences.
Ana (Product PM): Good — I'll draft 2 variants: one dev-focused, one exec-focused.
Jin (SRE): Quick ops question: for Dedicated SLAs, do we have the fallback policy spelled out? e.g., if pool degraded -> auto-fallback to hosted model with region routing. Need that for runbooks.
Raj (VP Product): Yes — fallback is policy-based. Short spec: canary -> primary -> fallback. We'll publish a one-page SLO/fallback summary in docs by end of next sprint.
Claire (CEO): Market focus note: we remain PLG-led but target customer motion varies: early AI-native startups (self-serve), mid-market (usage -> sales outreach), enterprise (Dedicated/Private + contracts). Mention APAC expansion as "growing" not GA everywhere.
Ana (Product PM): Helpful. Can we have a single sentence for pitch decks about competitors? e.g., "Unlike X and Y, we combine a high-performance runtime with rollout and observability built-in." Want to avoid naming too many competitors.
Raj (VP Product): That's a good neutral line. Use generic terms: "managed endpoints" and "self-hosted runtimes" and then our sweet spot: "unified runtime + ops-first ergonomics."
Sam (Staff Engineer): Quick follow: are we open-sourcing any of the runtime bits? that question always comes up in community threads.
Claire (CEO): We will open-source select tooling and libs (SDKs, some benchmarks). Core runtime remains proprietary for now. We can put a short FAQ line: "select components open; managed runtime offered for production."
Jin (SRE): For the runbooks, any change to error-handling policies? should the oncall switch to "auto-failover" mode by default?
Emily (Director, Eng): Ops SRE proposal: default route = region-primary, then tiered fallback. Oncall retains manual override. We'll add a /runbook snippet.
Ana (Product PM): Timeline ask: when can the marketing site & internal playbook be updated?
Raj (VP Product): Marketing copy updates in two weeks. Internal playbook + runbooks in 3 weeks. I'll coordinate with growth and SRE.
ops-bot: Recording and slides uploaded: https://redwood-inference.slides/ah-2050001111 :spiral_notepad: 
Claire (CEO): Thanks everyone. I'll join the doc review on Friday 10am PT.
Ana (Product PM): Great — I'll send calendar invite and draft the two copy variants. :thumbsup:
Sam (Staff Engineer): +1 on the docs. want the short tech blurb for the benchmarks page.
Emily (Director, Eng): I'll add a short non-technical blurb for marketing.
Jin (SRE): I'll prep the runbook PR.
Raj (VP Product): Closing note: emphasize "predictable inference economics" as a lead message.
Ana (Product PM): Noted. Thanks all — I'll post drafts in #product later today.
thread_text_summary: Follow-up thread from all-hands clarifying mission framing (serving vs model ownership), messaging for marketing vs developer docs, Dedicated SLAs and fallbacks, open-source stance, timelines for copy and runbooks, and action owners.
